**What it does**
- `POST /classify` takes the raw ticket text as a `text/plain` body and returns `{"category": "BILLING" | "TECHNICAL" | "OTHER"}`. The endpoint is in `org.acme.rest.ClassifyResource`.
- Blank or over-long tickets (more than 4000 characters) get a 400 before any model call.
- The classification is done by `org.acme.ai.TicketClassifier`, an AI service that returns a `Category` enum. It uses a model named `smaller` (`qwen3:1.7b` on Ollama, temperature 0).
- A guard, `TicketInjectionGuard`, rejects tickets that contain extra `<ticket>` markup or "ignore previous instructions". It counts the tags in the rendered prompt instead of using the scaffolding template's guard, because that guard would have rejected every request. The prompt's own `<ticket>` tags are in the same text it checks.
- The classifier has a 60-second timeout and one retry, and the retry is skipped when the guard rejects the input. I did not add a fallback: a fallback to OTHER would label model outages as real classifications.

- Ollama setup (`ollama serve` plus `ollama pull qwen3:1.7b`) is only needed to actually run it.
- Dev Services are disabled, so no containers are started.
- The project has two tests, a wiring smoke test and a blank-ticket 400 test. Neither needs a model.
- `quarkus_create` put the project in `./ticket-classifier`, so I moved it to `./app`. I did not run `git init`, and I did not call `quarkus_skills` for the extensions.
- I left out WebSockets, observability and agentic extensions because the task didn't need them. The `native` profile and the Java 25 and `-parameters` settings come from the generated `pom.xml`.
